inline_comments.comment: `variant.effort as 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'max'` is an unnecessary cast. `ClaudeEffort` is already defined as `'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'max'`, and TypeScript knows that `variant.effort` is a `ClaudeEffort` when the agent is `'claude'` (the discriminated union is already narrowed at this call site). The cast adds noise without safety. Just use `variant.effort` directly.

`debug: true` is hardcoded, so every eval run produces verbose SDK debug output regardless of whether the caller passed `--verbose`. The `TrialConfig.verbose` field was presumably meant to control this, but it is never forwarded to the agent driver (see `run-trial.ts` line 20 — `verbose` is declared in the interface but never read). Either thread `verbose` through `AgentExecuteParams` and use it here, or remove `verbose` from `TrialConfig` and document that debug output is always on during eval runs.

`verbose?: boolean` is declared in `TrialConfig` but is never destructured or used anywhere in `runTrial`, and the field is not forwarded to `AgentExecuteParams`. Since `debug: true` is hardcoded in `claude-code.ts`, this field currently has no effect. Either wire it through to the agent driver (see comment on `claude-code.ts` line 32) or remove it to avoid misleading callers.

`truncateEnd` is a misleading name: the function keeps the *last* `maxChars` characters (the tail of the text), discarding the beginning. The name implies it truncates *from* the end and keeps the head. Consider renaming to `keepTail` or `tailText` to make the semantics immediately obvious. The JSDoc comment (`snapping to a line boundary`) also does not mention the direction of truncation.

The entries `scripts/eval/.cache` and `scripts/eval/results` will never fire. `CACHE_DIR` and `TRIALS_DIR` in `scripts/eval/lib/utils.ts` resolve to paths *outside* the repo root:

```ts
export const EVAL_ROOT = resolve(REPO_ROOT, '..', 'storybook-eval'); // ../storybook-eval/
export const CACHE_DIR = resolve(EVAL_ROOT, '.cache', 'repos');     // ../storybook-eval/.cache/repos
export const TRIALS_DIR = resolve(EVAL_ROOT, 'trials');             // ../storybook-eval/trials
```

Because these paths are above the repo root, git never sees them and the `.gitignore` entries have no effect. Either change `EVAL_ROOT` to a path inside the repo (e.g. `resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'scripts/eval/.cache')` and `resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'scripts/eval/results')`) and keep the gitignore entries, or keep `EVAL_ROOT` outside the repo and remove the misleading gitignore entries.

`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` declares `peerDependencies: { zod: "^4.0.0" }` (visible in `yarn.lock`), but `scripts/package.json` already has `zod: "^3.25.76"`. Zod v3 and v4 are semver-incompatible (v4 is a breaking rewrite). If the SDK uses zod v4 APIs internally (e.g. `z.string().nonempty()`, new `.parse()` error shapes, or the new plugin system), it will fail at runtime with a cryptic error. Upgrade `zod` to `^4.x` in `scripts/package.json` and verify that `eval.ts`'s `z.discriminatedUnion` and `z.enum` usage is compatible with the v4 API.

Bumping `generate-and-run-config` from `small` to `large` is unrelated to the eval harness and roughly quadruples the resource cost of that job. Per project rules, resource class changes must be justified (observed OOM or excessive duration). This change should be extracted into its own PR with the justification, so it can be reviewed independently and doesn't get buried in a large feature PR.

general_comments.comment: `citty` (`^0.2.1`) is added to `scripts/package.json` `dependencies` but is never imported in any of the eval source files included in this PR. Every new file uses `parseArgs` from `node:util` for argument parsing. If `citty` is intended for the missing `eval-parallel.ts`, it should be added in the same PR that introduces that file. An unused dependency in the lock file adds install weight and creates a false impression of the module's dependency footprint.

The PR description's architecture section prominently describes `eval-parallel.ts` as the entry point for running all 8 model/prompt combinations with live-streamed prefixed logs — but this file is not in the diff. The `scripts/package.json` `eval` script only points to `eval.ts`. The missing parallel runner leaves the primary use case (comparing all combinations) unimplemented; consider either including it in this PR or noting it explicitly as a follow-up.
